Quantities of a Quadratic Penalty for a Marginal Criterion

Source: R/generics.R
penalty_matrix.Rd

These functions return the four quantities that a REML or marginal likelihood criterion requires from a quadratic penalty. penalty_matrix() returns the matrix \(S(\theta)\) of the quadratic form, penalty_rank() its rank, penalty_null_basis() an orthonormal basis of the directions that the penalty leaves unpenalized, and penalty_logpdet() the log pseudo-determinant with its first two derivatives in the hyperparameters.

Usage

penalty_matrix(pen, theta, ...)

penalty_rank(pen, ...)

penalty_null_basis(pen, ...)

penalty_logpdet(pen, theta, ...)

Arguments

pen

A penalty() object for which is_quadratic() is TRUE, or a separable penalty for penalty_null_basis().

theta

A named list of hyperparameter values, or a named numeric vector carrying the same. Only penalty_matrix() and penalty_logpdet() take this argument.

...

Passed to methods. The shipped methods do not read it.

Value

penalty_matrix() returns a symmetric q x q matrix, where q is pen@n_coef. penalty_rank() returns a single integer, fixed at construction. penalty_null_basis() returns a q x (q - r) matrix with orthonormal columns spanning the null space, and a q x 0 matrix when there is none. The two matrices are base matrices ordinarily, and dgCMatrix objects for a penalty built by quadratic_penalty() with blocks > 1. penalty_logpdet() returns a list of three: value, a single number; grad, a named list of one number per hyperparameter; and hess, a named list of one number per hyperparameter pair, keyed as in penalty_hess_theta(), with the diagonal pairs first.

Role in a marginal criterion

A marginal criterion integrates the coefficients out under the prior that the penalty defines, and a Laplace expansion at the penalized mode leaves \(\tfrac{1}{2}\log^{+}\lvert S(\theta)\rvert - \tfrac{1}{2}\log\lvert H + S(\theta)\rvert\). These generics supply the first term. It is a pseudo-determinant, taken only over the range of \(S\), because a smoothing penalty is rank deficient by design and its ordinary determinant is zero.

The rank and the null basis are fixed at construction and do not move with theta, so penalty_rank() and penalty_null_basis() do not take it. A count of the eigenvalues of the assembled \(S(\theta)\) above a tolerance would fall as several smoothing parameters spread apart, whereas the null space of a sum of positive semidefinite matrices is the intersection of their null spaces and does not depend on the weights.

The log pseudo-determinant

For the plain quadratic branch \(S = \lambda D^\top P D\) and

$$\log^{+}\lvert S \rvert = r\log\lambda + \log^{+}\lvert D^\top P D \rvert,$$

with \(r = \operatorname{rank}(D^\top P D)\), so the gradient is \(r/\lambda\) and the second derivative \(-r/\lambda^2\), both exact and both returned. For the structured branch the value and the derivatives are those of the log-determinant of the parameters7 matrix parameter (parameters7::param_logdet() and its derivatives). All are on the parameter scale, and there is no scale argument.

Branches that supply them

The quadratic, structured and additive branches, for which is_quadratic() is TRUE, supply all four. For a separable penalty (distrib_penalty()), penalty_null_basis() returns an orthonormal basis of the null space of the map, the directions of \(\beta\) on which the penalty does not depend, and the other three signal an error. For SCAD, MCP and any other branch without a method of its own, all four signal an error with a message that names is_quadratic().

Methods

The four methods on the base class penalty() signal an error with a message that names is_quadratic(), because a penalty that is not quadratic has no matrix, rank, null basis or log pseudo-determinant. The quadratic branches register their own methods, documented at penalty_matrix.QuadraticPenalty(), penalty_matrix.StructuredPenalty() and penalty_matrix.AdditivePenalty(), and a separable penalty registers penalty_null_basis.DistribPenalty().

See also

is_quadratic() for the predicate that determines which branches supply these, quadratic_penalty(), structured_penalty() and additive_penalty() for those branches, penalty_hess_theta() for the names of penalty_logpdet()'s hess.

Examples

# Second differences over four coefficients give rank 2 and a
# two-dimensional null space that holds the level and the slope.
pen <- quadratic_penalty(crossprod(diff(diag(4), differences = 2)))
penalty_rank(pen)
#> [1] 2
N <- penalty_null_basis(pen)
dim(N)
#> [1] 4 2

# The matrix annihilates that basis exactly.
max(abs(penalty_matrix(pen, list(lambda = 2)) %*% N))
#> [1] 1.332268e-15

# And a straight line, which the null space spans, costs nothing.
penalty_gradient(pen, c(1, 2, 3, 4), list(lambda = 2))
#> [1] 0 0 0 0

# The log pseudo-determinant is r log(lambda) plus a constant, so its
# derivatives are r/lambda and -r/lambda^2.
lp <- penalty_logpdet(pen, list(lambda = 2))
c(lp$grad$lambda, lp$hess$lambda_lambda)
#> [1]  1.0 -0.5
c(penalty_rank(pen) / 2, -penalty_rank(pen) / 4)
#> [1]  1.0 -0.5

# A separable penalty under a second-difference map has a null basis,
# and no matrix.
lsep <- lasso_penalty(map = diff(diag(4), differences = 2))
dim(penalty_null_basis(lsep))
#> [1] 4 2
try(penalty_matrix(lsep, list(lambda = 1)))
#> Error : Only a quadratic penalty exposes its matrix; see is_quadratic().
